disclaimer.title: Educational and research use only
disclaimer.short: Educational and research demonstration only — not a diagnosis.
disclaimer.full: This application is for educational and research demonstration only. Its predictions are based on the supplied dataset and are not a diagnosis or a substitute for professional medical evaluation.
disclaimer.predict: The number below is a statistical model output on 1988 Cleveland Clinic research data. It is not a diagnosis, not a calibrated personal risk, and must not be used for screening, triage or treatment decisions.

performance.title: Model performance
performance.subtitle: All figures are measured on a stratified, held-out 20% test split ({n} patients) that the models never saw during training.
performance.rocDesc: True positive rate vs false positive rate across all thresholds
performance.limits: Recall (sensitivity) is the share of disease-present patients the model catches; specificity is the share of disease-absent patients it correctly clears. In cardiac screening a missed case is usually costlier than a false alarm, so a lower threshold would trade specificity for sensitivity. With only {n} test patients these numbers carry wide uncertainty, and strong test-set performance is not proof of clinical reliability.
metric.accuracy.desc: Share of all test patients classified correctly.
metric.precision.desc: Of patients predicted class 1, the share truly class 1.
metric.recall.desc: Of true class 1 patients, the share the model found.
metric.roc_auc.desc: Ranking quality across every threshold (0.5 = chance).

compare.title: Model confidence is not clinical risk
confidence.title: Model confidence
confidence.what: How decisively the model picks its class for this record, judged only against the 1988 research data. It describes the model, not the patient.
risk.title: Clinical risk
risk.body: A person's real heart risk depends on their full history, examination and validated clinical tools used by a doctor. This app cannot and does not estimate it.
plain.title: What this means in plain language
plain.score: The model gives this record a score of {p}. Records scoring 50% or more are placed in dataset class 1, so this one is placed in class {cls}.
plain.confidence: Its confidence in that call is {c}: {level}.
plain.level.weak: the score is close to the 50% line, so a small change in any input could flip the class
plain.level.moderate: a moderate lean, but not a clear-cut separation
plain.level.strong: a strong lean — this record looks much like one class in the training data
plain.factors: What moved the score most, compared with a typical patient in the data:
plain.meaning: These are patterns the model learned from 303 research patients. They show how the model reacts, not what causes heart disease, and they are not medical advice.

landing.title: Heart disease prediction, explained — on real research data
landing.subtitle: CardioSense is an academic machine-learning prototype built on the 303-patient UCI Cleveland dataset. Score records live, screen whole CSV files, and inspect honest test-set performance.
landing.f.predict.title: Live prediction
landing.f.predict.body: Adjust 13 clinical inputs and watch the model output update instantly, with plain-language explanations.
landing.f.batch.title: Bulk CSV screening
landing.f.batch.body: Upload a file, get row-level validation and a scored CSV back — processed in memory only.
landing.f.perf.title: Honest evaluation
landing.f.perf.body: Accuracy, recall, ROC curves and confusion matrices from a real held-out test split.
landing.f.data.title: Real dataset
landing.f.data.body: Browse all 303 anonymized research records and load any case into the predictor.

landing.f.lang.body: Use the app in English, Spanish or Hindi.
landing.f.safety.title: Built for safety
landing.f.safety.body: Model confidence is never presented as clinical risk or a diagnosis.
